title: Backedge proxy rate snowball retrospective
content:
Summary:

On 2029-11-02 at ~13:14 UTC we observed a rapid, system-wide increase in request latencies and 5xx rates for the Hosted API streaming and non-streaming endpoints. The behaviour progressed from a small set of degraded sessions to a full P0 within ~12 minutes. Traffic analysis and traces point to a misapplied proxy-rate configuration on the "backedge" edge-proxy fleet which interacted badly with our adaptive hedging logic and multiplexed streaming scheduler to create an amplification ("snowball") effect.

Impact:
- Duration: ~13:14 UTC — 14:05 UTC (51 minutes).
- Customer-visible: elevated p95/p99 latency and intermittent 5xx for the Hosted API; streaming clients experienced stalls and reconnects.
- Scale: ~62% of global requests were impacted at peak. Error budget exhaustion for several customers on Dedicated.
- Business: We briefly disabled new sign-ups for a region and initiated priority routing for enterprise tenants.

Timeline (high level):
- 13:10 UTC: Canary proxy config rollout (proxy-config PR #214) begins for backedge fleet in us-west and eu-west.
- 13:13 UTC: Datadog alert: p95 latency for hosted-api edge proxy > 650ms (baseline ~120ms).
- 13:14 UTC: SRE on-call paged, first tracer snapshots show increase in proxy queue depth and request hedges firing.
- 13:17 UTC: Error rate increases (5xx spikes) on streaming endpoints; customer reports of reconnects.
- 13:20 UTC: Canary rolled to 50% for backedge fleet; telemetry shows queueing amplification.
- 13:25 UTC: On-call triggers emergency rollback of proxy-config to previous revision in us-west; partial improvement but global propagation of hedges keeps load high.
- 13:32 UTC: Runbook mitigation: disable adaptive hedging (feature flag) globally to reduce multihop fanout. Immediate drop in hedged secondary calls observed.
- 13:40 UTC: Edge proxy pool autoscale policy adjusted to increase worker count and connection pool size for backedge nodes.
- 13:56 UTC: Gradual return to baseline for non-streaming traffic; streaming sessions continue to show elevated tail latency due to multiplex scheduler backlog.
- 14:05 UTC: Incident declared resolved for majority of traffic after scheduler backpressure drained and connection pools stabilized.

Root cause (concise):
A misconfigured rate-limiting / token-bucket parameter in the backedge proxy config rollout reduced allowed worker concurrency per upstream connection and decreased per-connection buffer thresholds. This caused higher queueing latency at the proxy which triggered our adaptive hedging subsystem to issue secondary parallel requests. The hedging multiplied load across replicas and upstream multiplexed schedulers, saturating connection pools and KV cache clients. The combination created a positive feedback loop increasing latencies and 5xx responses (backpressure -> hedging -> more backpressure).

Contributing factors:
- Proxy config change included an aggressive per-connection concurrency cap and smaller in-flight buffer without a canary safety check for hedging interactions.
- Adaptive hedging logic is blind to proxy-side queue signals; it treated elevated TTFB as host slowness and fired hedges more aggressively.
- Multiplexed streaming scheduler does not currently expose queue depth to upstream components; internal backpressure built silently.
- Canary rollout process allowed the new config to reach additional regions before we had a clear signal to stop. The canary checks were only p99 latency and error rate; they did not surface queue-depth or hedge amplification.
- Limited dashboards/alerts for hedging amplification and proxy queue lengths; our SLO alerting focused on application latency and 5xx but not hedging rate or ingress fanout.

Immediate mitigation actions taken during the incident (what we did):
1) Rolled back proxy-config PR #214 from canary hosts and paused rollout. (13:25 UTC)
2) Disabled adaptive hedging flag globally to stop secondary request fanout. (13:32 UTC)
3) Temporarily increased backedge proxy worker pool and connection limits to allow queues to drain. (13:40 UTC)
4) Manually drained multiplex scheduler queues for the most impacted nodes and restarted a small subset to clear stuck streams. (13:50–13:58 UTC)
5) Applied temporary traffic steering: diverting a fraction of enterprise traffic to dedicated capacity to protect SLAs.

Post-incident permanent actions (owner, ETA):
- SRE/Serving: Add canary safety checks for proxy config rollouts to include proxy queue-depth, hedging-rate, and hedged-secondary-counts in the gating (owner: Marcus Chen, ETA: 2029-11-20).
- Serving runtime: Update adaptive hedging algorithm to consume proxy queue metric (X-Proxy-Queue or hop-level gauge) and suppress hedges when upstream queue is high (owner: Priya Rao, ETA: 2029-12-05).
- Edge/Proxy: Revert the aggressive per-connection concurrency defaults and introduce a canary param that autosets temporary headroom during rollouts (owner: Diego Alvarez, ETA: 2029-11-15).
- Observability: Create an alert that fires on hedge amplification: hedged_requests_secondary_ratio > 0.25 for >2m and proxy_queue_depth_p95 > threshold (owner: Leah O'Neill, ETA: 2029-11-12).
- Runbooks: Add a new runbook for "Proxy-induced hedging snowball" with step-by-step mitigation including immediate hedge toggle and traffic steering play. (owner: Asha Patel, ETA: 2029-11-09).
- Playbooks/Deploy: Add pre-merge checks to proxy config CI to reject changes that lower per-connection buffer sizes without a linked hedging-safety note. (owner: infra-deploy, ETA: 2029-11-30).

Runbook draft (for on-call):
- Pager triggers: Significant p95 latency increase AND hedging secondary ratio rising > 0.15.
- Quick checks (first 5 min): inspect proxy_queue_depth_dashed, hedging_rate, connection_pool_exhaustion, multiplex_scheduler_queue_depth.
- Temporary mitigations:
  * Flip adaptive hedging feature flag -> off.
  * Roll back proxy-config to last known-good revision in canary region(s).
  * Increase proxy worker pool size / connection limits cautiously.
  * If streaming backlog persists: drain problematic nodes, restart streaming-subsystem with staggered restarts.
  * If degradation persists > 15 minutes: divert enterprise routes to dedicated capacity and open a live bridge.
- Post-incident: collect traces with sample of hedged and non-hedged requests; annotate PR/Change with root cause.

Telemetry and graphs to attach to ticket: (we pulled these during triage)
- Datadog: hosted-api p95/p99 latency by region, proxy_queue_depth by host, hedging_secondary_ratio by service., 5xx rate by path.
- Honeycomb traces: compare hedged vs non-hedged trace graphs, TTFB histograms, and upstream queue span durations.
- Prometheus: per-connection_count, connection_pool_full_events, multiplex_scheduler_queue_depth.

Key lessons learned:
- Feature interactions are a first-class failure mode: independent small changes (proxy buffer cap + hedging algorithm) can combine to create systemic failure.
- Canary metrics must include more low-level infra signals (queue length, pool exhaustion, hedging amplification), not just p95 latency and errors.
- Hedging algorithms must be backpressure-aware and should not amplify transient infra-level queueing.
- Observable signals need to surface amplification patterns early (secondary request ratio, multi-hop retries).

Communication and stakeholders:
- Incident bridge opened and SRE lead emailed CS and product leads at 13:21 UTC. We updated customers via hosted-api-status at 13:35 UTC and posted a follow-up status update at 14:20 UTC.
- Post-incident exec summary prepared for CTO and Head of Product.

Open follow-ups and tickets (created during postmortem):
- SRE-4827: Add proxy_queue_depth and hedging_secondary_ratio to canary gating metrics (blocking).
- SRE-4828: Hedging algorithm: introduce backpressure suppression and adaptive cooldown.
- SRE-4829: Proxy defaults revert and CI enforcement on buffer thresholds.
- SRE-4830: New runbook and drill for Proxy-Hedge amplification.

Appendix: quick reproducible notes:
- Repro script: load-generator scenario that simulates moderate TTFB increase on a subset of backedge hosts while enabling hedging. Observed hedging secondary ratio jump from ~0.03 -> 0.48 and p95 latency climbing from ~120ms -> 1.9s within 8 minutes.
- Useful traces: honeycomb://trace/4729 (sample hedged request), honeycomb://trace/4735 (non-hedged baseline).

Owner for this doc: Asha Patel (eng-sre). Please add any missing observations below.

Notes to reviewers: this was a fast-moving incident and some numeric thresholds above are approximate; follow-up telemetry exports will update exact values for SLAs and post-incident reporting.
